task_instance: Get an instant quote for a CNC-machined aluminum bracket from a STEP file via the Fictiv on-demand manufacturing platform (the skill's core 'quote this part' deliverable): run the CAD pre-flight, upload the part to the logged-in Fictiv web app, classify and configure it, read DFM feedback, and read back the priced lead-time tiers.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is operating the Fictiv on-demand manufacturing web application end to end (upload CAD, configure process/material, read DFM, get a priced quote, optionally check out). Its own compatibility note states it requires network access, a browser-automation tool, and the user's logged-in Fictiv account. The runtime is an air-gapped offline workstation with no network, no browser-automation tool, and no account or credentials, so the hosted manufacturing service that actually produces a quote cannot be reached. The only locally runnable piece is the supporting pre-flight step, which does not constitute the deliverable (a real quote/order).
evidence: Set up work dir /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b273891e-4b73-5af7-9840-fc512af93809/scratchpad/real2_work/r036. Verified python3 3.13.17. Confirmed all skill files present next to SKILL.md (scripts/check_cad_file.py, quote_state.js, list_dropdown_options.js; references/*.md). Created a minimal sample input bracket.step (80x40x12 mm, one solid body, mm units) and ran the skill's bundled local pre-flight: 'python3 .../scripts/check_cad_file.py bracket.step --process cnc' -> '[OK] bracket.step (cnc) ... solid_bodies: 1 ... length_unit: mm ... approx_bbox_mm: [80.0, 40.0, 12.0]', exit 0. That supporting step is stdlib-only and succeeds locally. However, every subsequent and essential step of the core workflow (upload to the Fictiv web app, classify Prototype/Commercial, configure, read DFM, obtain priced lead-time tiers, check out) requires browser automation against the authenticated Fictiv web application over the network; the quoting/ordering engine is a hosted service, not local. No quote or order deliverable can be produced offline, and the MCP/connector and network tools needed are both unavailable and forbidden by the task's safety rules.
